cruxes.question: Does confounding bias in Western cohorts operate toward null (healthy user bias) or away from null (unmeasured dietary pattern confounding)?
Is the inverse association in Chinese Kadoorie a true population-specific effect or artifact of reverse causality and different dietary context?
Are the three US cohorts (NHS, HPFS, NHANES/MESA) truly independent replications or do they share sufficient methodological structure that failure of one measurement assumption collapses all three?

evidence_streams.label: NHS/HPFS prospective cohorts (null effect)
evidence_streams.weakness: FFQ-based dietary cholesterol measurement with moderate validation (r=0.4-0.6); healthy user bias in healthcare worker populations; self-reported CVD outcomes in some analyses; loss to follow-up; unable to identify hyper-responders
supports: Does confounding bias in Western cohorts operate toward null (healthy user bias) or away from null (unmeasured dietary pattern confounding)?
Are the three US cohorts (NHS, HPFS, NHANES/MESA) truly independent replications or do they share sufficient methodological structure that failure of one measurement assumption collapses all three?

evidence_streams.label: NHANES/MESA positive association
evidence_streams.weakness: Cross-sectional component in NHANES; FFQ dietary cholesterol proxy identical to NHS/HPFS; confounding by overall diet quality not fully disentangled; outcome ascertainment methods differ from NHS/HPFS; residual confounding likely inflates effect
supports: Does confounding bias in Western cohorts operate toward null (healthy user bias) or away from null (unmeasured dietary pattern confounding)?
Are the three US cohorts (NHS, HPFS, NHANES/MESA) truly independent replications or do they share sufficient methodological structure that failure of one measurement assumption collapses all three?

evidence_streams.label: Chinese Kadoorie inverse association
evidence_streams.weakness: Different population with different genetic cholesterol absorption profiles; dietary pattern context not comparable to Western cohorts; potential reverse causality (ill individuals reduce egg consumption); outcome ascertainment methods differ; smaller effect size; mechanistic explanation absent
supports: Is the inverse association in Chinese Kadoorie a true population-specific effect or artifact of reverse causality and different dietary context?

evidence_streams.label: Mechanistic hyper-responder studies
evidence_streams.weakness: Small N; short duration; controlled feeding does not address CVD outcomes; selection bias in volunteer populations; LDL-C elevation does not establish CVD causation; does not identify who hyper-responders are in population cohorts; ~25% prevalence estimate unvalidated in prospective cohorts
supports: Does confounding bias in Western cohorts operate toward null (healthy user bias) or away from null (unmeasured dietary pattern confounding)?

evidence_streams.label: PREDIMED RCT (Mediterranean diet cardioprotective)
evidence_streams.weakness: Eggs not isolated as variable; multivariate intervention (Mediterranean diet includes olive oil, nuts, fish, whole grains); adherence heterogeneous; 5-year follow-up short for CVD outcomes; does not address eggs in isolation or in Western dietary context
supports: Does confounding bias in Western cohorts operate toward null (healthy user bias) or away from null (unmeasured dietary pattern confounding)?

correlated_pairs.shared_assumption: FFQ-derived dietary cholesterol is a valid proxy for actual egg intake and dietary cholesterol consumption. Both cohorts use identical or near-identical FFQ instruments and dietary cholesterol calculation methods.
correlated_pairs.implication: If FFQ systematically misclassifies egg consumers (e.g., underreporting in health-conscious subgroups, overreporting in less health-conscious subgroups), both cohorts fail in the same direction simultaneously. The apparent disagreement (null vs. positive) may reflect different confounding structures operating on the same flawed measurement, not true replication. This reduces effective independence from 3 independent cohorts to 1.5 independent measurement approaches. Effective evidentiary weight should be discounted by ~40-50% from what naive pooling would suggest. If FFQ error is random rather than systematic, both cohorts are attenuated equally, biasing aggregate estimate toward null.

correlated_pairs.shared_assumption: Residual confounding by unmeasured factors (genetic variation in cholesterol absorption, statin use, subclinical atherosclerosis at baseline, dietary pattern context) operates similarly across both cohorts and can be adequately controlled by adjustment for measured confounders (age, sex, smoking, BMI, physical activity).
correlated_pairs.implication: If residual confounding differs systematically between cohorts (e.g., NHS/HPFS has stronger healthy user bias pushing toward null; NHANES/MESA has stronger unmeasured dietary pattern confounding pushing toward positive), the apparent disagreement is not a true contradiction but a reflection of different confounding structures. This means neither cohort provides an unbiased estimate of the true effect. The aggregate estimate becomes a weighted average of two biased estimates in opposite directions, which may appear more certain than either alone. Effective confidence should be reduced by ~30-40%.

correlated_pairs.shared_assumption: The effect of egg consumption on CVD risk is homogeneous across populations, or differences are explained by measured confounders (age, sex, smoking, BMI, diet quality). Population-specific genetic variation in cholesterol absorption and dietary pattern context are either absent or adequately captured by diet quality adjustment.
correlated_pairs.implication: If true population heterogeneity exists (Chinese populations have different APOE allele frequencies, different baseline LDL-C levels, different dietary pattern contexts for egg consumption), pooling NHS/HPFS and Kadoorie produces a meaningless aggregate estimate. The inverse association in Kadoorie and null in NHS/HPFS would indicate true interaction, not disagreement. Pooling would obscure the true structure. If heterogeneity is real, the aggregate probability estimate should be stratified by population, not collapsed to a single range. Current pooling approach inflates apparent certainty by ~25-35%.

calibrated_estimates.hypothesis: Consuming 1 egg/day increases CVD risk in healthy US adults (NHS/HPFS baseline population)
calibrated_estimates.conditions: Assumes confounding is adequately measured and controlled; assumes FFQ dietary cholesterol is a valid proxy; assumes no unmeasured genetic variation in cholesterol absorption; assumes healthy user bias dominates over unmeasured dietary pattern confounding; excludes individuals with existing CVD, familial hypercholesterolemia, or metabolic dysfunction at baseline

calibrated_estimates.hypothesis: Consuming 1 egg/day increases CVD risk in US general population (NHANES/MESA)
calibrated_estimates.conditions: Assumes residual confounding by overall diet quality is partially unmeasured; assumes FFQ dietary cholesterol measurement is valid; includes metabolic dysfunction and subclinical atherosclerosis; assumes confounding bias operates away from null (unmeasured dietary pattern confounding dominates); does not account for potential reverse causality in cross-sectional component

calibrated_estimates.hypothesis: Consuming 1 egg/day decreases CVD risk in Chinese populations (Kadoorie Biobank)
calibrated_estimates.conditions: Assumes inverse association is real and not artifact of reverse causality; assumes different dietary context (eggs + rice vs. eggs + refined carbs) explains divergence from Western cohorts; assumes genetic variation in cholesterol absorption differs between populations; does not account for potential selection bias in outcome ascertainment or loss to follow-up

calibrated_estimates.hypothesis: Eggs are harmful for CVD (aggregate across all populations, unweighted)
calibrated_estimates.conditions: Assumes bidirectional confounding is partially unmeasured; assumes population heterogeneity is real but not dominant; assumes FFQ measurement error is random rather than systematic; assumes no true interaction by population; does not account for hyper-responder subgroup (estimated ~25% of population) who may experience larger effects

calibrated_estimates.hypothesis: Eggs are harmful for CVD (aggregate across US populations only, weighted by N and accounting for methodological correlation)
calibrated_estimates.conditions: Assumes NHS/HPFS and NHANES/MESA share ~60% of methodological structure (FFQ measurement, confounding patterns) and thus provide ~1.6 independent evidence streams rather than 2; assumes confounding direction is ambiguous and bidirectional; assumes residual confounding is partially unmeasured; excludes Chinese Kadoorie due to population heterogeneity; does not account for hyper-responder subgroup

calibrated_estimates.hypothesis: True effect of eggs on CVD is null or inverse in healthy populations, positive in metabolically dysfunctional populations (population-stratified model)
calibrated_estimates.conditions: Assumes true population heterogeneity exists and is not explained by confounding; assumes NHS/HPFS represents healthy population (null effect 15-30%); assumes NHANES/MESA represents metabolically dysfunctional population (positive effect 40-55%); assumes Chinese Kadoorie represents different genetic/dietary context (inverse effect 5-20%); assumes aggregate estimate is misleading and stratified estimates are more valid

settled: Eggs contain dietary cholesterol and can raise LDL-C in some individuals (mechanistically established in controlled feeding studies)
Large prospective cohorts (NHS, HPFS) show no strong association between 1 egg/day and CVD events in healthy healthcare worker populations
PREDIMED demonstrates that Mediterranean diet patterns (which include eggs) are cardioprotective, but eggs are not isolated as the causal variable
Population heterogeneity exists: Chinese Kadoorie shows inverse association while Western cohorts show null to positive association
performed_as_settled: The three US cohorts (NHS, HPFS, NHANES/MESA) constitute independent replication and can be pooled to tighten confidence intervals — actually, they share FFQ measurement methodology and confounding structures, reducing effective independence

Confounding is adequately measured in all cohorts — actually, residual confounding by genetic variation, medication use, and dietary pattern context is unmeasured and likely operates in opposite directions across cohorts

FFQ-derived dietary cholesterol is a valid proxy for actual intake — actually, FFQ validation studies show moderate correlation (r=0.4-0.6) with biomarkers, and systematic misclassification by health consciousness is plausible

The null effect in NHS/HPFS is the true effect — actually, healthy user bias may push this estimate toward null, while unmeasured dietary pattern confounding in NHANES/MESA may push that estimate away from null; true effect is ambiguous

Hyper-responder subgroup is clinically irrelevant because population average is null — actually, if ~25% of population experiences 50-70% increased risk, this is clinically important but invisible in population averages
